subject: Harlem Park Three
query: where are the harlem park three now
title: Where are the Harlem Park Three now? HBO's When a Witness Recants
answer: The Harlem Park Three, Alfred Chestnut, Ransom Watkins and Andrew Stewart, were freed on Nov. 25, 2019, after 36 years in prison for a 1983 Baltimore killing they did not commit. Maryland awarded each man about $2.9 million in 2020, and Baltimore agreed in October 2023 to pay $48 million to settle their lawsuit.
body:
The three were arrested on Nov. 24, 1983, at age 16, after a 14-year-old student was killed at Harlem Park Junior High School in Baltimore, and were convicted on May 28, 1984, and sentenced to life. Their convictions rested on testimony from teenage witnesses that the documentary says was coerced. Their release in 2019 followed the discovery of police reports that had been withheld; Baltimore City Circuit Judge Charles Peters freed them.

In August 2020 the men sued the Baltimore Police Department and officers who worked the case. The city's Board of Estimates approved the $48 million settlement on Oct. 18, 2023; each man was to receive about $14.9 million.

Their story is the subject of "When a Witness Recants," directed by Dawn Porter, with Ta-Nehisi Coates as an executive producer. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on Jan. 27, 2026, is based on a New Yorker story by Jennifer Gonnerman, and debuts on HBO Max on Nov. 17, 2026.
in_the_news: HBO's documentary "When a Witness Recants," about the Harlem Park Three, premieres on Nov. 17, 2026.
